title: Extension of Surveillance Cameras to Private Estates to Prevent High-rise Littering
what_it_is: Extension of Surveillance Cameras to Private Estates to Prevent High-rise Littering

sections.label: Littering enforcement actions count
sections.summary: Last year, 32,000 enforcement actions were taken against littering offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Last year, it took 32,000 enforcement actions against littering offenders.

sections.label: May clean-up event participation
sections.summary: A month-long May event saw over 370 organisations join more than 500 clean-up activities islandwide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The month-long event held in May this year saw more than 370 organisations, including grassroots organisations, public agencies and corporations, taking part in more than 500 clean-up activities across the island.

sections.label: Private estates ownership and access
sections.summary: Private estates are collectively owned by residents and public access to them is restricted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Unlike public estates, private estates are collectively owned by their residents and public access to such estates are restricted.

sections.label: Condominium by-laws against littering
sections.summary: Many condominiums have by-laws prohibiting littering within their estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Many condominiums have already put in place by-laws prohibiting littering within their estates.

sections.label: Littering law covers public places
sections.summary: The Environmental Public Health Act's prohibition against littering applies to publicly accessible places only.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the difference in treatment, let me say that the prohibition against littering under our current law, the Environmental Public Health Act applies to publicly accessible places only.

sections.label: NEA enforcement and MCST collaboration
sections.summary: NEA cannot enforce littering within private estates but may collaborate with MCSTs on high-rise littering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And NEA is, in turn, unable to carry out enforcement against littering incidents within these private estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: However, when a Management Corporation Strata Title (MCST) approaches NEA for assistance to tackle cases of high-rise littering, NEA will explore ways to collaborate with them, to educate and advise the residents against such anti-social acts, for instance, working with them to send out advisory notices against such anti-social acts.

sections.label: Private estate by-laws enforcement
sections.summary: Residents should foster collective responsibility, management corporations can apply to Courts to enforce by-laws, and there are no plans to extend anti-littering laws to private estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For private estates where access is largely restricted, in fact, to residents of family members and their friends, it will be best for residents to work together to foster collective responsibility and cultivate the right positive social norms and behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But if all else fails, the management corporation can apply to the Courts to enforce these by-laws against errant residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Amending our legislation to extend our anti-littering laws to private estates would likely illicit negative reactions, such as it being intrusive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we currently have no plans to amend our current legislation.
